items.title: 52060_Eddie Barefield oral history interview
items.q: I worked with him -- what year? Oh, even after I recorded with him in -- in the late '30s or first of the '40s, whatever it was, I came back with him again, with Pearl Bailey, when he was conducting for Pearl Bailey.

ctx.x: Well, you know, they always talk about how, you know, he -- his band never really got the acclaim that it should have gotten, and then of course, at first, when he wrote for Benny Goodman, Benny Goodman's band got --

Right. Yeah, because he -- all of the things that he recorded in the '20s, Benny Goodman came back and got famous on them in the '30s. Don Redmon was another great musician. In fact, I worked with him -- what year? Oh, even after I recorded with him in -- in the late '30s or first of the '40s, whatever it was, I came back with him again, with Pearl Bailey, when he was conducting for Pearl Bailey. I forget what year -- years those were.
